title: A.M.B. AND OTHERS v. SPAIN - [English Translation] by European Roma Rights Centre "ERRC"
summary: In the case of A.M.B. and Others v. Spain, the applicant, Mrs. A.M.B., a Spanish national of Roma origin, brought a complaint to the European Court of Human Rights on behalf of herself and her two minor children against the Spanish state. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Traveller families facing eviction from social housing without adequate safeguards or alternative accommodation, a situation that can exacerbate social exclusion and hardship for already marginalised communities. Mrs. A.M.B. and her children had been living since July 2009 in an uninhabited flat owned by the Madrid Housing Institute (IVIMA), after repeated unsuccessful requests for official housing. In February 2011, IVIMA ordered their eviction without offering alternative housing, and subsequent legal proceedings confirmed the expulsion, despite the applicant’s arguments about her family’s precarious situation and Roma identity. The applicant alleged violations of Article 3 (prohibition of inhuman or degrading treatment) and Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life) of the European Convention on Human Rights, particularly due to the lack of alternative accommodation and the non-suspensive effect of her appeal. However, the Court declared the application inadmissible under Article 35, as domestic remedies had not been exhausted—the applicant’s constitutional appeal was still pending in Spain. This case underscores the procedural barriers Roma and Traveller families may face in seeking protection from eviction, reflecting broader challenges in accessing justice and adequate housing in Europe.
